text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Egerton University in the Rift Valley closed indefinitely after police shoot dead a first-year student during the second day of riots over a refund the students were demanding.
- A South African Air Force plane will deliver 18 tonnes of food to famine-stricken north eastern district of Wajir.
- An inmate escapes from a coffee farm he was working in after stripping naked and leaving the prison uniform hanging from a tree before fleeing.
- Sources close to opposition party FORD-Kenya's disciplinary committee say faction leader Raila Odinga has been struck off the party register.
- Chief Justice Abdul Majid Cockar calls for a medical report on the health of one of Koigi wa Wamwere co-convicts alleged to be sick at the Kamiti Maximum Prison in Nairobi.
- Construction companies in Kenya complain that tough requirements by the World Bank will prevent them from bidding for the building of the Nairobi/Mombasa highway.
- A widow loses case over 60 acres of prime land valued at over 100 million shilllings to a local bank for failing to pay a loan of 45 million advanced to her by the bank.
